morning_soundtrack.title: The record-breaking, genre-melting, career-redefining evolution of Miranda Lambert
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Lambert started out as a scrappy country singer with a me-against-the-world attitude. How did she end up making lush disco songs and writing one of the biggest pop hits of the year?
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The sound of a woman kicking off her boots, trading rhinestones for sequins, and daring you to say something about it.

morning_soundtrack.title: Dave Grohl Joins AC/DC For “Highway To Hell” In New Jersey
morning_soundtrack.snippet: On Friday (Oct. 2) in New Jersey, Foo Fighters filled in for the Pretty Reckless for a second time on AC/DC's Power Up tour. When the Australian rock legends played their hit "Highway To Hell," they brought out Dave Grohl for help.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The kind of moment that makes grown adults lose their minds and throw their fists in the air without a single apology.

morning_soundtrack.title: AC/DC and Foo Fighters Deliver Epic Night of Rock ‘n’ Roll at MetLife Stadium: Review, Photos, Video + Setlists
morning_soundtrack.snippet: The two Rock & Roll Hall of Fame acts joined forces for an unforgettable show in New Jersey. AC/DC and Foo Fighters Deliver Epic Night of Rock ‘n’ Roll at MetLife Stadium: Review, Photos, Video + Setlists Spencer Kaufman
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Stadium concrete vibrating under your feet while 80,000 strangers become your closest friends for exactly three hours.

morning_soundtrack.snippet: With a special introduction from AOC and Bernie Sanders, the show brought together multiple eras of indie rock. The Strokes’ Homecoming Concert in NYC with Beach House, TV on the Radio, and Fcukers Was Indie Music Heaven: Recap + Videos Paolo Ragusa
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Like finding every dog-eared page of your college music diary brought to life on a single sweaty, euphoric New York night.

morning_soundtrack.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall Is a Brilliant Portrait of an Artist Frozen in Time: Review
morning_soundtrack.snippet: The Paul Thomas Anderson-directed concert film captures the young songwriter in action with patient, hypnotic focus. Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall Is a Brilliant Portrait of an Artist Frozen in Time: Review Paolo Ragusa
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Still and reverent, like watching someone write in a journal through a rain-streaked window — beautiful precisely because they don't know you're there.

global_silver_linings.title: Fan ‘Storms Out’ as Team Loses on TV, Only to Become Hero for Woman Stuck in Mud Chest-high
global_silver_linings.snippet: Just after Alastair Cass stormed out of his house because his football team lost he become a hero for a woman in dire need of a win—to save her life. The 40-year-old left home in “frustration” after his beloved Arsenal team was hammered by Brighton 3-0. When he got outside, he heard a woman’s cries […]
global_silver_linings.reason: A moment of frustration turned into an act of genuine courage, reminding us that everyday heroes often show up in the most unexpected circumstances. Sometimes the best thing a bad game can do is send someone outside at exactly the right moment.

global_silver_linings.title: Florida zoo captures adorable moment when a newborn baby sloth meets his dad
global_silver_linings.snippet: If you thought adults sloths were cute, wait 'til you see this baby.
global_silver_linings.reason: A baby sloth meeting his father for the first time is a tender reminder that new life and family bonds exist in all corners of the animal kingdom. Conservation efforts at zoos make moments like this possible, and that's worth celebrating.

featured_read.title: Lit Hub Weekly: September 28 – October 3, 2026
featured_read.snippet: “Chalk it up to stubbornness. McGuane is as committed to his vision as his characters are to theirs.” Why Thomas McGuane is writing the most vital literature of the Trump Era.​| Lit Hub Politics Jason Bell recounts the secret three-man
featured_read.blurb: Thomas McGuane has spent decades writing characters too ornery to compromise, and this essay argues that stubbornness, right now, is exactly the literary virtue America needs. A case for why one aging novelist's refusal to soften might be the most honest response to the present moment.

reading_room.title: The Mainstreaming of Anti-Indian Bigotry
reading_room.snippet: A Republican schism over a social-media post by a Texas politician revealed that the party’s defense of a color-blind meritocracy has its limits.
reading_room.blurb: A single social-media post by a Texas politician cracked open a fault line in the Republican Party's cherished 'color-blind meritocracy' argument—and what spilled out was uglier than the usual talking points. This piece traces exactly where that myth breaks down, and for whom.

reading_room.title: What Vienna Lost When It Lost Its Jews
reading_room.snippet: Douglas Smith’s The City Without Jews revisits the decimation of a robust community—and the city that betrayed it.
reading_room.blurb: Vienna was remade into one of modernity's great cultural capitals partly by its Jewish community—and then it watched, and often helped, as that community was erased. Douglas Smith's history asks the quietly devastating question of what a city owes the people it betrayed.

reading_room.title: How Sugar from Outer Space Became One of the Backbones of Life on Earth
reading_room.snippet: Is there life elsewhere, or is Earth unique in the universe? This is one of humanity’s great unanswered questions. One way to approach this mystery is to investigate how life began here on Earth.
reading_room.blurb: Ribose, a sugar essential to RNA, has been found in meteorites—meaning the raw ingredients of life may have rained down on early Earth from space, which reframes the question of life's origins from 'how did it start here?' to 'how far does it travel?' A genuinely mind-rearranging piece of science writing.

reading_room.title: What It Feels Like at Cornell Right Now
reading_room.snippet: "I began to do what I do — reading and writing and thinking about misogyny—because of my dismay at how girls and women are treated on campus, and at other college campuses across America."
reading_room.blurb: A scholar of misogyny turned her attention to her own campus and found the patterns she'd spent a career studying playing out in real time among her students. This is an essay about what it costs to keep looking clearly at something that never seems to change.

reading_room.title: Here’s what’s making us happy  this  week.
reading_room.snippet: This week, your friendly neighborhood Lit Hub staff is feasting on a narrative diet—but not in the stacks you’d expect. October brings fresh appreciation for the time-bound object. I’m talking about the kind of art you can imbibe on your
reading_room.blurb: The Lit Hub staff makes a gentle argument for the time-bound art object—the thing you have to show up for before it's gone—as a quiet antidote to the everything-forever nature of modern consumption. Consider it an invitation to pay attention differently this October.
